documents.unit: Office of Academic Affairs / OTS / Student Affairs
documents.title: Policy on Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence at TSU (Policy No. 1.09)
documents.date_or_term: effective upon approval (board committee item April 28, 2025)
documents.summary: TSU's board-approved policy lets faculty decide whether and how students use AI in each course, while stating that AI doing a student's work is prohibited unless faculty allow it and it is cited. It also sets data restrictions, prohibited uses, enforcement through the Code of Conduct, oversight offices, review and training.
documents.stance_why: The policy says "Faculty may elect to allow students to use AI for particular assignments" and gives faculty "the authority and responsibility to set course-specific AI policies", so the decision is handed to instructors. It also says students "may be permitted" to use AI and that AI doing the work is "strictly prohibited unless allowed by course faculty", but these defaults sit under the instructor election, so delegates.

units.why: The purpose says the policy ensures "compliance with Tennessee law, data security, privacy laws, and ethical standards" while promoting AI use. That states the purpose and principles of an institution-wide framework, so P56.
units.anchor: promoting the effective use of artificial intelligence

units.why: The scope clause says the policy "applies to faculty, staff, students, and employees" using AI for "academic, research, or administrative purposes". It sets who and what the framework covers, so P56 (scope) rather than P61, which is for definitions.
units.anchor: applies to faculty, staff, students, and employees who use AI tools

units.why: Defines "Artificial Intelligence (AI)" as "Machine-based systems that can ... make predictions, recommendations, or decisions". A definition that sets what the policy covers, so P61.
units.anchor: Machine-based systems that can, for a given set of human-
units.frag_end: formulate options for information or action.

units.why: Defines Generative AI as "AI that generates new content, such as text, images, and code". It is a definition setting the policy coverage (explicitly including code), so P61.
units.anchor: AI that generates new content, such as text, images, and code

units.why: Defines "Fair Use" as a legal doctrine permitting unlicensed use of copyrighted works for teaching and research. It is a copyright definition supporting the later fair-use rule, so P52 (copyright) rather than P61, which defines AI.
units.anchor: permitting the unlicensed use of copyright-protected works in certain circumstances

units.why: The University "embraces the integration of AI with a commitment to scholarly rigor". That is an institutional welcome of AI use as a default posture, so P02 with encourage stance; informs because it is a statement of position, not an instruction.
units.anchor: The University embraces the integration of AI

units.why: Says AI "poses unique challenges to academic integrity, while also offering exciting possibilities that will enhance teaching and student engagement". The benefit half names benefits for learning, so P87.
units.anchor: exciting possibilities that will enhance teaching and student engagement
units.frag_end: evolving landscape of learning and professional endeavors.
units.fit_note: Also names the integrity challenge and preparation for the professional landscape, which P87 does not capture.

units.why: States "Students may be permitted to use AI tools for assistance with coursework." It is a default permission for students (conditional "may be permitted"), so P02 with may.
units.anchor: Students may be permitted to use AI tools for assistance with coursework.

units.why: "Students are expected to review, validate, and understand the output from these tools." Verifying output is P31; the "understand" element is secondary, so P31 not P30.
units.anchor: Students are expected to review, validate, and understand the output

units.why: "Faculty may elect to allow students to use AI for particular assignments or according to specified guidelines." The decision is made per faculty member and assignment, so P04.
units.anchor: Faculty may elect to allow students to use AI for particular assignments

units.why: "Students should contact course faculty for any questions concerning the faculty AI election". Students unsure of the rule are told to ask the instructor, so P10.
units.anchor: Students should contact course faculty for any questions
units.frag_end: use of GAI in each course.

units.why: "the use of AI to complete assignments, write papers, or answer quiz questions on behalf of the student is strictly prohibited unless allowed by course faculty". This bans having AI produce submitted work, so P19. The "unless allowed" fallback is also present, but the core rule is about AI doing the work, so P19 rather than P06.
units.anchor: strictly prohibited unless allowed by course faculty and appropriately cited
units.frag_end: by course faculty and appropriately cited.

units.why: "The improper use of AI constitutes a breach of academic integrity and is considered academic misconduct ... similar to plagiarism or cheating." Classifies misuse as misconduct, so P36.
units.anchor: considered academic misconduct under the Code of Student Conduct

units.why: The text says the work submitted by a student must be the student own work. This is the ownership rule for submitted work, so P29.
units.anchor: work submitted by a student must
units.frag_start: While AI can provide assistance, the
units.frag_end: must be the student's own work.
units.policy: Work submitted by a student must be the student's own work.

units.why: "Any use of AI-generated content should be clearly cited." Requires acknowledging AI use in the submission without tool/prompt detail, so P24.
units.anchor: Any use of AI-generated content should be clearly cited.

units.why: "Students must be mindful of what information they are sharing and always prioritize protecting personal and academic data." A duty to protect data, so P50.
units.anchor: Students must be mindful of what information they are sharing

units.why: "Students are advised to review University technology policies ... to ensure compliance with acceptable use policies." Points students to existing university policy, so P77.
units.anchor: Students are advised to review University technology policies and guidelines

units.why: "no student will be at a disadvantage for lack of access to AI technology." Assignments are designed so lack of access does not hurt students: equity of access, P51.
units.anchor: no student will be at a disadvantage for lack of access
units.frag_start: The University recognizes that not all
units.frag_end: lack of access to AI technology.

units.why: Faculty "have the authority and responsibility to set course-specific AI policies". Decision rests with instructors, so P04.
units.anchor: authority and responsibility to set course-specific AI policies

units.why: The same sentence says such policies must "clearly communicate to students the permitted uses, if any, of AI". Instructors must state expectations to students, so P09 (separate from P04, the decision itself).
units.anchor: clearly communicate to students the permitted uses, if any, of AI

units.why: "AI-generated content for University operations must be fact-checked". Governs AI use in administrative operations, so P76 (the fact-checking element is secondary).
units.anchor: AI-generated content for University operations must be fact-

units.why: "misidentifications can occur" with AI detection tools, so faculty "must exercise caution". Signals detector unreliability, P39 (caution rather than a ban).
units.anchor: Faculty must exercise caution with AI detection tools
units.fit_note: Calls for caution about detector error rather than saying detectors will not be used.

units.why: "AI detection results should not be the sole determinant of academic dishonesty." Detector output may support but not alone decide a finding: an evidence standard, P69.
units.anchor: AI detection results should not be the sole determinant

units.why: "Authors shall be fully responsible for ensuring the allowed use of any AI generated data". Responsibility for IP and copyright of AI output, so P52.
units.anchor: Authors shall be fully responsible for ensuring the allowed use

units.why: "AI technology is to be used in accordance with" codes of conduct, standards, university policies and applicable laws. A compliance rule, P77.
units.anchor: AI technology is to be used in accordance with

units.why: "The use of AI technology is subject to the University policies ... including the Information Security Policy, Policy No. 10.01." Subjects AI to existing IT policy, P77.
units.anchor: Information Security Policy, Policy No. 10.01.
units.frag_start: The use of AI technology is subject

units.why: "Before inputting Restricted Data into an AI tool, an OTS security review must be conducted." A data-protection gate before sensitive data goes into AI, so P50 (protect data) rather than P65, which is about reviewing tools for purchase or deployment.
units.anchor: Before inputting Restricted Data into an AI tool, an OTS

units.why: "Faculty, staff, and students are free to use any AI technology for instructional purposes so long as Restricted Data is not entered". A broad permission with one condition, P02.
units.anchor: free to use any AI technology for instructional purposes
units.frag_start: Restricted Data – Faculty, staff, and students

units.why: Restricted Data "may not be entered into AI tools unless approved by OTS" and includes FERPA-protected student records and grades. Data-protection prohibition, P50.
units.anchor: Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA)-protected information,

units.why: AI tools may not be used for "Generating misinformation, defamatory content, or academic dishonesty". A general conduct ban on deceptive use, P74.
units.anchor: Generating misinformation, defamatory content, or academic dishonesty;

units.why: AI may not be used for "Facilitating cybersecurity threats, malware, or phishing". Malicious use ban, P74.
units.anchor: Facilitating cybersecurity threats, malware, or phishing;

units.why: AI may not be used for "Violating copyright, intellectual property, or contract or licensing agreements". Intellectual-property rule, P52.
units.anchor: Violating copyright, intellectual property, or contract or licensing agreements;

units.why: AI may not be used for "Assisting in discriminatory practices, harassment, or illegal activities". Harmful-use ban, P74.
units.anchor: Assisting in discriminatory practices, harassment, or illegal activities.

units.why: "AI-generated content may be used for educational, research, or analytical purposes, provided it complies with copyright laws". A conditional permission tied to copyright, P52.
units.anchor: AI-generated content may be used for educational, research, or analytical purposes

units.why: Student violations "will be handled in accordance with the university Student Code of Conduct." Student violations go through the conduct process, P36.
units.anchor: Students – Violations of this policy will be handled in accordance with the
units.frag_end: Student Code of Conduct, as applicable.
units.fit_note: Names the Code of Conduct as the venue but does not itself call AI misuse misconduct or name penalties.

units.why: Faculty and staff violations "will be handled in accordance with the university normal disciplinary processes". Existing processes govern violations, P77.
units.anchor: normal disciplinary processes for faculty and staff

units.why: "OTS will monitor and block or restrict unauthorized AI tools" on university devices and network. Names the office that enforces tool restrictions, P80.
units.anchor: OTS will monitor and block or restrict unauthorized AI tools
units.fit_note: Also a restriction on unauthorized tools, not only naming an enforcing office.

units.why: "Regular policy reviews will be conducted by the Responsible Officials". Commits to periodic review, P54.
units.anchor: Regular policy reviews will be conducted by the Responsible Officials

units.why: "The Office of Risk and Financial Compliance shall be responsible for reviewing University procedures" and reporting. Assigns oversight, P80.
units.anchor: Office of Risk and Financial Compliance shall be responsible for reviewing

units.why: "TSU will provide: Workshops for faculty, staff, and students on AI ethics, security, and academic applications." Training for students and staff, so P70 (not P63, which is faculty-only).
units.anchor: Workshops for faculty, staff, and students on AI ethics, security

units.why: "Updated guidance on AI integration ... will be regularly provided." The institution commits to keep issuing guidance, nearest P54.
units.anchor: Updated guidance on AI integration in academic and administrative settings
units.fit_note: Commits to updated guidance for users rather than revising the policy itself.

units.why: "the TSU Board of Trustees is responsible for adopting a policy" under T.C.A. 49-7-185. States the legal basis and body that made the policy, P84.
units.anchor: the TSU Board of Trustees is responsible for adopting a policy

units.why: "The Board of Trustees charges the President and Responsible Offices with the University oversight". Names who oversees, P80.
units.anchor: charges the President and Responsible Offices with the University
units.frag_start: The Board of Trustees charges the

units.why: "This policy is subject to periodic review and updates." Provisional policy, P54.
units.anchor: This policy is subject to periodic review and updates.

documents.title: How should I use AI? - Artificial Intelligence (AI) LibGuide (TSU syllabus AI options)
tiers: Permitted under some circumstances or with explicit permission
Broader use permitted within specified guidelines
documents.summary: A library guide that relays the three TSU syllabus options (prohibit, permit with permission, broader use) with sample statements, and adds advice on convenience uses, AI research tools and the prompt-assess-cite habit. It is guidance, not the policy itself.
documents.stance_why: The guide says "TSU has three different ways that professors can integrate (or not integrate) AI into their syllabi" and gives three template statements, so it offers tiers and leaves the choice to instructors: delegates.

units.why: The scale "outlines the progression of learner engagement with AI tools in education". It describes levels of AI engagement (a spectrum), nearest P05, but it is a learner-development scale, not tiers of permitted use.
units.anchor: This spectrum outlines the progression of learner engagement with AI tools in education
units.fit_note: A spectrum of learner engagement, not named tiers of permitted use per assessment.

units.why: "TSU has three different ways that professors can integrate (or not integrate) AI into their syllabi." Names three syllabus options, so P05 (tiers) rather than P04, which is only that the instructor decides.
units.anchor: TSU has three different ways that professors can integrate (or not integrate) AI

units.why: Option 1 says "Generative AI including but not limited to ChatGPT is not permitted." A ban template for the course, P01.
units.anchor: Generative AI including but not limited to ChatGPT is not permitted.
units.frag_end: limited to ChatGPT is not permitted.

units.why: Option 1 gives the reason "Intellectual honesty is vital to an academic community and for fair evaluation of your work." Fairness and honesty rationale, P95.
units.anchor: Intellectual honesty is vital to an academic community

units.why: Use "will violate the University Code of Honor Policy and will be treated as plagiarism." Classifies prohibited use as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: will violate the University Code of Honor Policy and will be treated as plagiarism

units.why: Option 2: AI "allowed in specific situations and with explicit permission". Banned unless permitted, narrower than option 3; nearest P06 (explicit permission as fallback).
units.anchor: allowed in specific situations and with explicit permission
units.frag_start: The use of generative AI, including
units.fit_note: A tier template: AI allowed only in specific situations with explicit permission, rather than a rule for silent syllabi.

units.why: Option 2 says AI "must be used responsibly and with appropriate citation." Citation requirement, P24.
units.anchor: must be used responsibly and with appropriate citation

units.why: "you are encouraged to discuss your situation with the instructor of record" if in doubt. Ask before using, P10.
units.anchor: you are encouraged to discuss your situation with the instructor of record
units.frag_start: If you are in doubt as

units.why: "Any misuse or improper use of generative AI will be considered a violation of the University Code of Honor Policy and will be treated as plagiarism." Misconduct classification in option 2, P36.
units.anchor: Any misuse or improper use of generative AI will be considered a violation

units.why: Option 3: generative AI "is allowed for any assignment with the proper citation in this course." Broad default permission, P02.
units.anchor: is allowed for any assignment with the proper citation in this course.
units.frag_start: The use of generative AI, such

units.why: "You are responsible for fact checking statements composed by all generative AI models." Verify output, P31.
units.anchor: You are responsible for fact checking statements composed by all generative AI models.

units.why: Option 3 repeats that misuse "will be regarded as a violation of the University Code of Honor Policy and will be treated as plagiarism." Separate template, so coded again; misconduct classification, P36.
units.anchor: any misuse or improper use of generative AI will be regarded as a violation

units.why: "Students should not use AI outside of the parameters set by their instructor unless they ask permission first." Ask the instructor before going beyond the stated rules, P10.
units.anchor: Students should not use AI outside of the parameters set by their instructor
units.fit_note: Also says AI use stays within the instructor's parameters.

units.why: "they should remember to cite the AI. Instructors will have information on how they would like classes to cite". Citation required, instructor sets the format, P24.
units.anchor: they should remember to cite the AI.
units.frag_start: Depending on what is written in
units.frag_end: to cite and use the AI.

units.why: Suggests asking an AI to "subtract the numbers in column A from column B" in a spreadsheet. A permitted convenience use for calculation, P89 (data analysis) is nearest.
units.anchor: copy everything into a spreadsheet and ask an AI to subtract the numbers
units.fit_note: A convenience example (arithmetic in a spreadsheet), not analysis or visualization of data.

units.why: "AI search engines (like Perplexity.ai) are great places to start your search for information." Allows AI search for research as a starting point, P12 (search engine to understand) is nearest.
units.anchor: are great places to start your search for information.
units.frag_start: There are quite a few ways
units.fit_note: About starting research with AI search, not understanding course concepts.

units.why: "AIs have been known to hallucinate (make things up), so researchers should look at the resources that are cited." Tells users to check AI output, P31.
units.anchor: AIs have been known to hallucinate (make things up)

units.why: "P.A.C. It Up ... stands for prompt, assess, and cite." A three-step heuristic combining prompting, evaluating and citing; it fits no single type cleanly, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: stands for prompt, assess, and cite.
units.uncovered_note: A named mnemonic framework telling students to prompt, assess output, and cite when using AI.

notes: Policy 1.09 is the only official TSU policy; the libguide relays the three syllabus options and is not itself the policy. No school or computing-unit policy found. P.A.C. It Up is UNCOVERED. The libguide page date (Oct 23, 2026) is the guide's last-updated stamp.
